title: After 10 years in software development, I'm trying my hand at games. Here's my first attempt
author: edinsonjohender
selftext:
Hi everyone!

I've been a software developer for about 10 years, and a while ago I finally jumped into something I'd always wanted to try: making a video game. This is my first real attempt, built with the help of AI tools along the way.

It's called Overvolt Arena, a robot arena game where you survive waves of enemies until the boss shows up. The video is the fight against the first one, the Matriarch.

I know there's a lot I'm probably getting wrong. That's partly why I'm posting. I'd really like to meet people who are into making games with AI, hear what you think, and learn from those of you who've been at this longer than me. Honest feedback is very welcome, the kind and constructive kind especially 🙂

If you'd like to follow along, try it early or just chat about game dev, I've started a small Discord: [Discord ](https://discord.gg/bVbwT8UHV)

Thanks for watching!

comments.author: iagamedev_gsc
comments.body:
Gostei muito do seu trabalho. Muito bom. Se aceitar uma sugestão, na parte de luta do boss os míssil, estão gerando muita fumaça gera certa poluição visual. Talvez diminuir um pouco a fumaça ou diminuir o tamanho dela. 
A posição da câmera tb, parece fazer aumentar o tamanho, as animações de fumaça mais perto da câmera fica muito grande.

replies.author: edinsonjohender
replies.body: Thank you so much! Yours is the first comment I've received, and I'm really glad it's such good feedback (from where I stand xD). You're right, there's quite a lot of smoke. I'm thinking of adding an effects/smoke level option in the settings. Also, the trailer camera is modified, so it uses different angles from the actual game. I might put together a gameplay video so it's easier to see how it really looks.

comments.author: Delicious_Bid8579
comments.body:
Looks a great work :clap

How long to get until this point? I'm following similar trajectory and struggling to find spare time to work on it after my work day. I'm 39 and age is present. For sure if I was doing this when younger would be able to put more effort on it

replies.author: edinsonjohender
replies.body:
Thanks a lot for your comment, I really appreciate it!

What I'm going to tell you is just my truth, nobody else's. I'm working on this full time right now, I'm 33. I quit my job 2 months ago because my boss had crazy FOMO about AI and wanted at least 2 backend services a day, because he could build an app with GPT in one day (like anyone who doesn't code, the AI gives them an amazing UI, but you look at the code and you can break it in 2 minutes, and they just don't get it).

I'm telling you this so you have some context for what comes next. For about a month I've been working like 20 hours a day. I barely sleep and energy drinks are my best friends. I posted this at 5am Colombia time and I'm answering you at 9am. I slept like 3 hours and I'm going to keep going, because I feel the same passion and excitement I felt when I started programming.

I don't know if I can keep this pace for another month haha, and eventually I'll have to go back to looking for a job. But that gives you an idea of how much time this takes, and whether age is really the problem.

replies.author: Delicious_Bid8579
replies.body:
Very brave you! This exactly same feeling keeps always in my mind, but won't do that. I think we need to policy us that we don't need to rush. It's a hobby from the start, but we see it can become money sometime in the future, however need to keep feet grounded.

Side comment (maybe might sting you), and that I saw yesterday in other post the same thing, I've started a comics series about the game in parallel. Started curious to see what would be and man, that's amazing. And is helping a loot to consolidate and polish and game's main story and evolution's possibilities.

replies.author: edinsonjohender
replies.body:
Keeping your feet on the ground is the smart move. I'll probably burn out at some point haha, but for now I'm enjoying it a lot.

And no sting at all, that's a really good idea! My game doesn't have a story yet, it's just robots fighting in an arena, and a comic sounds like a great way to build the world and the characters. I'd love to see yours if you share it somewhere!

replies.author: Delicious_Bid8579
replies.body: Not yet hahaha. I decided to follow a 2d isometric 2:1 game,  similar to Clash of Clans. Hard part is fighting AI to generate the isometric design as expected. Had then to create several arts manually to get the result I've expected. Started 1 and half month ago and have not something to show yet. Decided focus in the comics for now (planning to publish in webtoons) to have community's feedback before going fully ahead with the game. Will be faster to get a feedback I believe

replies.author: KalElReturns89
replies.body: Don't burn yourself out, but it looks like you're doing a great job to be honest. You have talent for this.

replies.author: edinsonjohender
replies.body: Thank you, that really means a lot! I'll try not to burn out haha

replies.author: edinsonjohender
replies.body: Thank you so much! Really glad you like it

comments.author: CreativeProblem7803
comments.body: looks fun, the boss reveal looks quite epic. Not sure if the gameplay is matching the trailer quality though, seems like a 3d roguelite to me.

replies.author: edinsonjohender
replies.body: Thanks! Fair point, the trailer camera is more cinematic than the real game. It's an arena game where you fight waves of robots and then a boss, building your robot with different parts. I'll share a gameplay video soon so you can see how it actually plays.

comments.author: edinsonjohender
comments.body:
https://reddit.com/link/pgwyu2x/video/v7wpt5q0envh1/player

Here's a bit of real gameplay! It came out in hard mode because I jumped straight into the boss scene without leveling up my robot first xD

comments.author: KalElReturns89
comments.body:
Love this. Robot combat is such a fun sport to me, always loved watching it growing up.

There are not very many games that do it well, mostly 1 and a somewhat distant 2. Robot Arena 2 and Robot Wars: Extreme Destruction.

Now I see there's a Robot Arena 3, anyone know if it was good?

replies.author: edinsonjohender
replies.body: Thanks! I haven't played those games, but I'll check them out to see how they handled robot combat. Mine is an arena shooter where you fight waves of robots and bosses, and you build your robot with different parts.

comments.author: KalElReturns89
comments.body: If I had a gameplay suggestion from the video, I saw in the comments and the trailer above, I would say don't forget to include all the different types of robot weapons. Having lots of options, makes things fun. I see there are a lot of missiles, it depends on whether you want to go for realism or not, but you could have different kinds of shields, and you could make physical weapons more powerful to compensate for the abundance of missiles. You could also have an active defense system like a shield that you could hold up.

replies.author: edinsonjohender
replies.body: Thanks! I'm working on a shield system right now, each type looks different and it also changes depending on how you build your robot. Melee weapons like saws or hammers are a good idea too, I'll keep that in mind.

comments.author: joshbuildsstuff
comments.body: Looks great!  Are you doing all of the animation and rigging yourself?  As a software developer also starting to play around with game dev I've had trouble trying to generate good animations for non-humanoid like creatures.

replies.author: edinsonjohender
replies.body: Yes! I built my own separate tools for effects, HUD, models, etc. Each one is custom made, so I can really work on the details.
